title: Thursday, September 17, 2026

headline.title: “Price action is usually a lot better after FOMC.” That line was written on the prep sheet before the open yesterday, and this is what it looks like. Everything is green and the risk assets are leading: ARM +4.75%, AMD +3.20%, INTC +3.10%, MU +2.19%, NVDA +1.68%, with QQQ +1.41% and IWM +1.17%. The Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75–4.00%, the first increase since July 2023 — and the relief is not in the decision, it is in the dots.
headline.summary: The dot plot landed closer to one more hike than two, which is the half the market was not positioned for. Sixteen of eighteen participants expect another increase, but twelve of eighteen peg 2026 at an average of 4.125% — one more 25bp move — with only four seeing two. Futures had been leaning toward two by year-end. And the detail that says the most about this Fed: Warsh declined to submit a dot at all. A chair who will not place his own marker on the grid is telling you the committee's median is the signal and his guidance is not on offer. The tape read it as relief: gold +1.85%, bonds +0.76%, crude −2.25% — every part of that combination says less tightening ahead, not more.

darkpool.note: Carried forward from Tuesday night — no fresh tape for this session yet, and the positioning below has since been resolved by an event that went the market's way. Roughly $5B of S&P 500 tracker size printed after hours, all of it bid-side: VOO $1.8B, IVV $1.7B and SPY $1.5B stacked together, the seventh straight session an S&P tracker topped the whole board. That is index money repositioning into a decision rather than an opinion about any single name, and the lean-not-verdict caveat applies twice over on index flow. The mega-caps leaned the same way — NVDA, AMD, MSFT, AVGO and AAPL all printed at the bid the night before a near-certain hike — while MU and PLTR took the ask side instead. NVDA's $1.2B bid print was its third consecutive night as the board's largest single name, and the opposite side of Monday's $796M ask. Size working both sides of one name into a decision is a hedge being built, and the hedge was not needed: the dots came in at 4.125%, softer than futures were carrying. MU has taken over the top of cumulative flow at $4.9B (mixed), ahead of NVDA $4.3B (bid) and META $3.1B (ask) — and MU reports 9/30, the first hard number in an argument conducted so far entirely through essays and interviews. Bond money showed up too, in BGFI $372M (mixed), the night before the Fed convened.
